items.title: Section: Stillness and Insight Mutually Reinforce, Culminating in Transformation of the Basis

items.zh: 悟入道理。正修行者如如毘鉢舍那串習清淨增上力故，增長廣大；如是如是能生身心所有輕安奢摩他品，當知亦得增長廣大。如如身心獲得輕安，如是如是於其所緣心一境性轉得增長；如如於緣心一境性轉復增長，如是如是轉復獲得身心輕安。
items.en: For one who correctly practices, having entered into the principle: to whatever degree insight, through habituated purification, becomes empowered and expands, to that same degree the calm-abiding that generates all bodily and mental pliancy should also be known to expand. To whatever degree body and mind attain pliancy, to that degree one-pointedness of mind, with respect to its object, further increases; and to whatever degree one-pointedness of mind further increases, to that degree bodily and mental pliancy is further attained.

items.zh: 心一境性、身心輕安，如是二法展轉相依，展轉相屬。身心輕安、心一境性，如是二法若得轉依，方乃究竟。得轉依故，於所知事現量智生。
items.en: One-pointedness of mind and bodily-mental pliancy — these two states depend upon each other, mutually bound together. Bodily-mental pliancy and one-pointedness of mind — only once these two states achieve transformation of the basis do they reach their culmination. Because the basis is transformed, direct, unmediated wisdom regarding the object of knowledge arises.

items.title: Section: How to Know a Purifying-Conduct Object Has Been Perfected — Three Signs, Illustrated Through Impurity

items.zh: 問：齊何當言究竟獲得不淨觀耶？乃至齊何當言究竟獲得阿那波那念耶？答：以要言之，修觀行者於不淨觀正加行中，親近、修習、多修習故。若行、若住雖有種種境界現前，雖復觀察所有眾相，而住自性，不由加行，多分不淨行相顯現，非諸淨相。由於不淨善修習故，於能隨順貪欲纏處法，心不趣入、心不愛樂、心不信解，安住於捨，深生厭逆。當於爾時，修觀行者應自了知：我今已得不淨觀，我今已得所修果。齊此名為於不淨觀已得究竟。與此相違，當知名為未得究竟。
items.en: Question: To what point should one say contemplation of impurity has been genuinely perfected? Answer: In brief, through drawing near to, cultivating, and extensively cultivating correct practice within contemplation of impurity. Whether going about ordinary activity or abiding in seated practice, though various objects present themselves, and though one observes their every feature, one abides in that very nature — without effort, images of impurity predominantly appear, not images of attractiveness. Because contemplation of impurity has been well cultivated, with respect to states conducive to craving, the mind does not enter into them, does not delight in them, does not place confidence in them, but abides in equanimity, deeply and thoroughly repelled. At that time, the practitioner should know for himself: "I have now attained contemplation of impurity; I have now attained the fruit of this practice." To this point is contemplation of impurity said to be genuinely perfected. The reverse of this should be known as not yet perfected.

items.title: The Same Three Signs Applied to Loving-Kindness, Dependent Origination, Elemental Analysis, and Breath-Counting

items.zh: 如不淨觀，如是慈愍、緣性緣起、界差別、阿那波那念念，當知亦爾。於中差別者，謂多分慈心行相顯現，非瞋恚相。於能隨順瞋恚纏處法，心不趣入，乃至廣說。多分無常、苦、空、無我行相顯現，非彼常、樂、身見俱行愚癡行相。於能隨順愚癡纏處法，心不趣入，乃至廣說。多分種種界性、非一界性身聚差別相想顯現，非身聚想。於能隨順憍慢纏處法，心不趣入，乃至廣說。多分內寂靜想、奢摩他想顯現，非戲論想。
items.en: As with contemplation of impurity, so too with loving-kindness, dependent-origination contemplation, elemental analysis, and mindfulness of the in-breath and out-breath — the same should be known to hold. The difference lies only in this: for loving-kindness, images of a loving mind predominantly appear, not images of hatred … for dependent-origination contemplation, images of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and no-self predominantly appear, not the delusory images bound up with permanence, pleasure, and the view of a fixed self … for elemental analysis, images of the body as a composite of differentiated elements, not a single unified mass, predominantly appear, not the image of a solid mass … for mindfulness of the breath, images of inner tranquility and calm-abiding predominantly appear, not images of idle discursive thought.

items.zh: 於能隨順尋思纏處法，心不趣入，乃至廣說。

items.title: Section: Defining the Dual Operation of Calm-Abiding and Insight

items.zh: 問：齊何當言奢摩他毘鉢舍那二種和合平等俱轉？由此說名雙運轉道。答：若有獲得九相心住中第九相心住，謂三摩呬多。彼用如是圓滿三摩地為所依止，於法觀中修增上慧。
items.en: Question: To what point should one say that calm-abiding and insight operate together in equal union, whereby this is called the dual-operation path? Answer: When one has attained the ninth of the nine stages of mental abiding, namely equipoise. Relying on such perfected samādhi as one's basis, one cultivates superior wisdom within contemplation of phenomena.

items.zh: 彼於爾時，由法觀故，任運轉道，無功用轉，不由加行，毘鉢舍那清淨鮮白，隨奢摩他調柔攝受，如奢摩他道攝受而轉。齊此名為奢摩他、毘鉢舍那二種和合平等俱轉。
items.en: At that time, through contemplating phenomena, the path proceeds spontaneously, functioning without effort, not depending on application; insight becomes pure and radiant, gathered in and made pliant by calm-abiding, proceeding just as calm-abiding's own path is gathered in. To this point is it called calm-abiding and insight operating together in equal union.

items.zh: 由此名為奢摩他、毘鉢舍那雙運轉道。

items.title: Section: A Summary Verse Recaps One-Pointedness of Mind and Purifying the Obstructions

items.zh: 中嗢柁南曰：相、尋思、伺察，隨行有三門。義、事、相、品、時、理，六事差別。初相應加行，次串習、無緩、無顛倒、應時、解了、無厭足、不棄捨善軛，最後正加行，是九應當知，有二品差別。知自性、因緣，見彼諸過患，正修習對治，令障得清淨。
items.en: The middle summary verse says: Following mark, investigation, and examination — the practice has three gates; meaning, substance, characteristic, category, time, and principle — these are the differentiated six things. First, fitting practice; next, habituated and unslackening practice; undistorted and timely practice; understanding and insatiable practice; not abandoning the good yoke; and last, correct practice — these nine should be known, each with its bright and dark distinction. Knowing their own-nature and causes, seeing their dangers, correctly cultivating their antidotes — thus are the obstructions purified.

items.title: Section: The Fifth and Final Locus Opens — Cultivating Mental Engagement

items.zh: 云何修作意？謂初修業者始修業時，於如是所安立普遍相中，由一境性及淨諸障，離邪加行，學正加行。彼應最初作如是念：我今為證心一境性及斷喜樂，當勤修習四種作意。何等為四？一、調練心作意，二、滋潤心作意，三、生輕安作意，四、淨智見作意。
items.en: What is cultivating mental engagement? That is, when a beginner first takes up practice, within the universal marks thus established, through one-pointedness of mind and purifying the obstructions, he abandons wrong practice and learns correct practice. He should, from the very outset, reflect thus: "I now, in order to realise one-pointedness of mind and for delight in severance, should diligently cultivate four kinds of mental engagement." What are the four? First, the mental engagement of taming the mind. Second, the mental engagement of moistening the mind. Third, the mental engagement of generating pliancy. Fourth, the mental engagement of purifying wisdom and insight.

blocks.text: How calm and insight grow together until the basis is transformed, how one knows an object has been mastered, and when calm and insight work as one.

"To whatever degree insight expands, to that degree the calm that generates pliancy also expands." "One-pointedness of mind and bodily-mental pliancy depend upon each other." Only with the **transformation of the basis** do they reach their culmination; then "direct, unmediated wisdom regarding the object of knowledge arises".

When is impurity contemplation perfected? "Whether going about ordinary activity or abiding in seated practice", even when other objects present themselves, "images of impurity predominantly appear, without effort". Master Cháng Bǎi: in walking, standing, sitting, lying.
For loving-kindness, "images of a loving mind predominantly appear"; for breath, "images of inner tranquility and calm".

"When one has attained the ninth stage, equipoise", insight proceeds "spontaneously, without effort"; "insight becomes pure and radiant, gathered in and made pliant by calm". This is the "dual-operation path" (止觀雙運).
It recaps the three gates, six things, nine practices, and four obstructions.
A beginner reflects: "I now, in order to realise one-pointedness of mind and to sever attachment to worldly joy, should…"

quiz.q: Pliancy and one-pointedness "reach culmination only with transformation of the basis." How do the masters explain it?
options: Miào Jìng: transforming the aggregates, greed into non-greed; Cháng Bǎi: the storehouse consciousness transformed, ultimately into stainless consciousness
quiz.why: "Only once these two states achieve transformation of the basis do they reach their culmination." Venerable Miào Jìng: the aggregates one relies on are transformed — greed, hatred, delusion become their absence. Master Cháng Bǎi: the storehouse consciousness is relinquished and transformed, renamed ripening consciousness, ultimately becoming stainless consciousness.

quiz.q: "As pliancy grows, one-pointedness grows." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: progressing from access concentration to the first dhyāna, whose pliancy surpasses it
quiz.why: "To whatever degree body and mind attain pliancy, to that degree one-pointedness of mind further increases." Venerable Miào Jìng: progressing from access concentration to the first dhyāna — the first dhyāna's bliss of pliancy surpasses that of access concentration.

quiz.q: "Because the basis is transformed, direct wisdom arises." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: the object can't be found, nor the knowing mind — subject and object equal
quiz.why: "Because the basis is transformed, direct, unmediated wisdom regarding the object of knowledge arises." Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing the object cannot be found, and the knowing mind cannot be found — subject and object utterly equal — is called direct wisdom regarding the knowable.

quiz.q: At perfection of impurity contemplation, "without effort, images of impurity predominantly appear." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: no special effort — the impurity and skeleton images appear naturally
quiz.why: "One abides in that very nature — without effort, images of impurity predominantly appear, not images of attractiveness." Venerable Miào Jìng: no special effort needed — impurity contemplation, the skeleton image, simply appears naturally.

quiz.q: At perfection of loving-kindness, "images of a loving mind predominantly appear." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe it?
options: when provoked, anger doesn't stir — compassion appears instead
quiz.why: "As with contemplation of impurity, so too with loving-kindness, dependent origination, elemental analysis, and breath mindfulness." Venerable Miào Jìng: when someone provokes you, anger would normally arise, but now it doesn't stir — instead compassion appears.

quiz.q: When calm and insight "operate together in equal union" — the dual-operation path. When do the masters say this happens?
options: Miào Jìng: at the first through fourth fruits, in Mahāyāna at acceptance of non-arising; Cháng Bǎi: at the first fruit for Hearers, the first ground for Mahāyāna
quiz.why: "When one has attained the ninth of the nine stages, namely equipoise. Relying on such perfected samādhi, one cultivates superior wisdom within contemplation of phenomena." Venerable Miào Jìng: dual operation is when the first through fourth fruits are attained; in the Mahāyāna, acceptance of non-arising. Master Cháng Bǎi: for Hearers, attaining the first fruit; for the Mahāyāna, the first ground.

quiz.q: Cultivating engagement "for one-pointedness and 斷喜樂" — rendered "to sever attachment to worldly joy." How do the masters read it?
options: both read it as "delight in cutting" — joyfully training and cutting loathsome things, not cutting joy; the English reverses it
quiz.why: "I now, in order to realise one-pointedness of mind and to sever attachment to worldly joy, should diligently cultivate four kinds of mental engagement." Venerable Miào Jìng: one should be diligent, delight in training in the noble path, and cut off the world's loathsome things — that is 斷喜樂, not cutting off joy. Master Cháng Bǎi: no longer clinging to worldly rise and fall, wanting neither, with strong renunciation — that is 斷喜樂. The English reads it in the opposite direction.
